prompt: Why can the planner's `PlannerModel` be built and run on Linux, when its views cannot?
hint: Which framework does `@Observable` come from?

choices.text: Because it is a struct, and structs need no framework
choices.why: It is a class, `final class PlannerModel`.

choices.text: Observation is part of the Swift toolchain, not of SwiftUI
choices.why: Right. Only the views need SwiftUI, and so a Mac.

choices.text: Linux has a reduced copy of SwiftUI that covers models
choices.why: SwiftUI has no Linux version, reduced or otherwise.

choices.text: `@MainActor` lets it run without an Apple SDK
choices.why: `@MainActor` is about which thread calls it, not which platform.

prompt: What does `@ObservationIgnored` do to `lastSaved`?
hint: Section 03's last scene.

choices.text: It makes the property read-only
choices.why: The program writes it in the last scene.

choices.text: It stops the property being saved to disk
choices.why: Nothing in the model saves to disk; the attribute is about tracking.

choices.text: Writes to it notify no view
choices.why: Right: setting it printed nothing, because it is out of tracking.

choices.text: It hides the property from other modules
choices.why: That is access control; it is still `public`.

prompt: Why is the week's total `public var week: WeekTotal { … }` rather than a stored property updated after each change?
hint: Lesson 6 section 06.

choices.text: Computed from `plan` and `today`, it cannot fall behind them
choices.why: Right, and Observation tracks what it reads, so a view reading `week` is told when either changes.

choices.text: `@Observable` cannot track stored properties of a struct type
choices.why: It tracks `plan`, a struct, perfectly well.

choices.text: Computed properties are faster than stored ones
choices.why: They recompute on each read; the point is correctness.

choices.text: The compiler forbids stored properties in an observable class
choices.why: `plan` and `today` are stored.

prompt: When `today` moved on a week, which two of section 03's screens were told?
hint: Which closures read `today`, directly or through `week`?

choices.text: CourseListView and Header
choices.why: The course list read only course titles, which are in `plan`.

choices.text: CourseListView and WeekView
choices.why: The list was left alone; it read nothing that changed.

choices.text: WeekView and Header
choices.why: Right: the header read `today`, and `week` reads it too.

choices.text: All three, since `today` belongs to the model
choices.why: Observation tells readers of the property, not every holder of the object.

prompt: Marking `s3` done told `CourseListView`, which shows only course titles. Why?
hint: What did the closure actually read on the model?

choices.text: Observation tells every view on screen about every change
choices.why: The header was not told, so it is not every view.

choices.text: It read `model.plan`, and the change wrote a new `plan`
choices.why: Right. `plan` is one tracked property; a session changing inside it is a write to `plan`.

choices.text: Course titles are computed from the sessions
choices.why: They are stored in `courses`; nothing computes them.

choices.text: `markDone` calls `print`, which every view observes
choices.why: `markDone` prints nothing; the lines come from `onChange`.

prompt: In section 03's output, how many screens were told when `lastSaved` was set?
hint: Count the lines under that scene.

prompt: In the program's output, `WeekView` and `Header` came out in one order. On another run, could they come out in the other?
hint: Section 03 says what Observation promises about order.

choices.text: No: they come out in the order the closures were registered
choices.why: The output already contradicts that: `WeekView` was registered after the list, before the header, and still came out first.

choices.text: Yes: Observation keeps no order among the views it notifies
choices.why: Right, which is why nothing in an app should depend on it.

choices.text: No: alphabetical order decides it
choices.why: Nothing sorts them by name.

choices.text: Only if the program is built in Release
choices.why: The build configuration has nothing to do with notification order.

prompt: Why does `PlannerApp` keep the model as `@State private var model = PlannerModel(…)`?
hint: `App` is a struct, made again when SwiftUI wants.

choices.text: So SwiftUI watches the object for changes
choices.why: Watching is Observation's job, in any `body` that reads a property.

choices.text: So one instance survives every new copy of the struct
choices.why: Right. Without it each copy would create a fresh model and lose the plan.

choices.text: Because classes may only be stored in `@State`
choices.why: Views store the same model in a plain `let`.

choices.text: To make the model private to the app's first screen
choices.why: It is passed or put in the environment for every screen.

prompt: `CourseListView` receives the model as `let model: PlannerModel`. How does it get redrawn when the plan changes?
hint: What subscribes a view?

choices.text: It does not; a `let` never changes, so neither does the screen
choices.why: The reference never changes; the object it points to does, and `body` read it.

choices.text: The parent passes a new model after each change
choices.why: There is one model for the life of the scene.

choices.text: Its `body` read `model.plan`, so Observation tells SwiftUI to run it again
choices.why: Right: reading the property is the subscription, whatever wrapper holds the reference.

choices.text: It needs `@ObservedObject`, or it is never redrawn
choices.why: That is the older mechanism, for `ObservableObject`, section 08.

prompt: To make `$model.today` from a model it was handed, a view declares it `@___ var model: PlannerModel`.
hint: The wrapper that adds a projected value and nothing else.

prompt: What does `@Bindable` add to a view's reference to an observable model?
hint: It neither owns nor watches.

choices.text: Ownership, so the model survives a redraw
choices.why: That is `@State`.

choices.text: A subscription to every property of the model
choices.why: Subscription comes from `body` reading properties.

choices.text: The `$` projection, to hand out bindings
choices.why: Right: `$model.today` becomes a `Binding<String>`.

choices.text: A copy of the model the text field edits
choices.why: No copy: the binding writes the shared model's `today`.

prompt: `WeekView` declares `@Environment(PlannerModel.self) private var model`, and a preview shows it without `.environment(model)`. What does Apple's documentation say happens?
hint: It is not a compile error.

choices.text: The preview gets a default `PlannerModel()`
choices.why: Nothing makes one for you.

choices.text: The build fails with a missing-environment error
choices.why: It compiles; the failure is at run time.

choices.text: The view shows empty values until a model arrives
choices.why: That is what asking for an optional lets you write yourself.

choices.text: SwiftUI throws an exception and the app stops
choices.why: Right; ask for `PlannerModel?` where the object may be absent.

prompt: A `SessionRow` needs one session and nothing else from the model. Which is the better way to give it the session?
hint: Section 06's two rules.

choices.text: A property in its initialiser, from its parent
choices.why: Right: one child, one value, visible where the row is made.

choices.text: `@Environment(PlannerModel.self)`, and look the session up by id
choices.why: It works, and it hides where the data comes from and makes every preview supply the model.

choices.text: A new `PlannerModel()` inside the row
choices.why: That is a second owner with an empty plan.

choices.text: A global variable the app sets at launch
choices.why: A global is invisible to SwiftUI and to Observation's subscriptions through views.

prompt: Match each situation in the planner to what the view should write.
hint: Who creates it, who changes it, how far away is the reader.

pairs.left: `WeekView` reads the model, several levels down
A row changes one session its parent owns
A section remembers whether it is expanded

prompt: Why does `SessionForm` keep its half-typed session in its own `@State` instead of writing straight into the model?
hint: Who else needs a session that is not saved yet?

choices.text: Text fields cannot bind to an observable model
choices.why: They can, through `@Bindable`, section 05.

choices.text: Until it is saved it belongs to nobody else
choices.why: Right; writing each keystroke into the plan would show a half-typed session on every screen.

choices.text: The model is read-only outside `PlannerApp`
choices.why: The detail screen calls `model.markDone` from outside it.

choices.text: `@State` is faster to type into
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

prompt: Which of these makes a second owner? Choose all that apply.
hint: Two plans in one app.

choices.text: A detail screen that copies its `plan` argument into its own `@State`
choices.why: Yes: from then on its plan and the list's are separate.

choices.text: `@Bindable var model: PlannerModel` in the week screen
choices.why: No: it holds the shared reference and adds `$`.

choices.text: `let model = PlannerModel(plan: Plan(), today: …)` inside a view
choices.why: Yes: a fresh model with an empty plan, not the app's.

choices.text: `@Environment(PlannerModel.self)` in two different screens
choices.why: No: both take out the one model the app put there.

prompt: With the older `ObservableObject`, which views run `body` again when one `@Published` property changes?
hint: What is a view subscribed to there?

choices.text: Only those that read that property
choices.why: That is what `@Observable` gives, as section 03 measured.

choices.text: Every view that holds the object
choices.why: Right: the object announces a change and every holder redraws, whatever it read.

choices.text: None until `objectWillChange` is called by hand
choices.why: `@Published` calls it for you.

choices.text: Only the view that created the object
choices.why: Views that received it with `@ObservedObject` redraw too.

prompt: A view declares `@ObservedObject var model = OldPlannerModel()`. What goes wrong?
hint: `@ObservedObject` does not keep anything.

choices.text: It does not compile, because an initial value is not allowed
choices.why: It compiles, which is why the mistake survives.

choices.text: The model is shared by every screen by accident
choices.why: The opposite: each redraw of the parent makes another one.

choices.text: A new model is created whenever the parent redraws, and its state is lost
choices.why: Right: `@StateObject` is the wrapper that creates and keeps.

choices.text: Combine refuses to publish from a view
choices.why: Publishing works; the object just does not live long.

hint: Section 08's table.

hint: From the field to the redraw.
items: Observation calls `onChange` for every view that read `today`

prompt: A screen that reads any part of `model.plan` redraws on any change to it. When is that worth fixing?
hint: Section 03's last paragraph.

choices.text: At once, in every app, since any extra redraw is a bug
choices.why: For a few dozen sessions nobody can see the cost, and simplicity is worth more.

choices.text: When a measured screen is slow, a list of thousands of rows
choices.why: Right: then split the state into pieces each screen reads separately.

choices.text: Not ever: Observation already tracks each session separately
choices.why: It tracks `plan` as one property, as the second scene showed.

choices.text: Only when the model is not `@MainActor`
choices.why: The actor decides the thread, not what is tracked.
